anchors.name: IESBA Code technology revisions
anchors.issuer: International Ethics Standards Board for Accountants (IESBA)
anchors.binding: Revisions to the IESBA Code of Ethics for professional accountants, approved in April 2023 and effective from December 2024.
anchors.asks: The five fundamental principles apply whatever tool is used. Accountants assess whether a technology's output is fit for purpose, including its limitations, data quality and bias, and guard against automation bias.
anchors.evidence: Registers and drafts in which every field or line links to its source page, approved by a named person before use.

anchors.name: IESBA staff paper on emerging technologies
anchors.asks: Opacity, non-determinism and data dependence can threaten the fundamental principles, so accountants need appropriate human oversight when evaluating technology-driven outputs. IESBA's June 2026 snapshot adds that professional responsibility cannot be delegated to a machine.
anchors.evidence: Drafts that a named person approves or rejects, with each decision logged.

anchors.name: FATF Recommendations 22 and 23
anchors.binding: International standards for countries (FATF Recommendations, as amended).
anchors.asks: Accountants who do certain client work, such as managing client money or assets, or creating, operating or managing companies and trusts, must do customer due diligence and keep records (R.22(d)). R.23 extends internal controls and suspicious-transaction reporting to them.
anchors.evidence: A register of trust deeds and company documents, each field linked to its page, for the person who makes the due-diligence decision.

anchors.name: IAASB technology initiative
anchors.binding: A board initiative; the AI material it is developing will be non-authoritative.
anchors.asks: How ISQM 1, ISQM 2 and ISA 220 apply when firms use AI tools, including approving and monitoring the tools.
anchors.evidence: Test records for each AI tool a firm approves, and a re-test after each change.

anchors.name: PCAOB staff spotlight on generative AI
anchors.binding: A staff view, not a Board rule.
anchors.asks: Reports that firms mainly used generative AI for administration and research, expected it to support people rather than replace them, and saw a need for strong supervision.
anchors.evidence: Drafts a named reviewer approves before use, with each decision logged.
